tasks.short: Review work orders and specifications to determine required materials and part types.

steps.what: Retrieve the correct work orders and specifications for the coil variant
Derive required material quantities and part types from released job specifications
Review material requirements against coil specifications and resolve unusual variants
Record confirmed material requirements and unresolved specification questions

tasks.design: Configure a released material-structure view and contextual preparation note in {OPS_SYSTEM}, linked to specifications in {DOCS}. The operator verifies variant requirements and records unresolved issues; nothing selects substitute materials or changes equipment automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: The operator may repeatedly derive quantities and rewrite job identifiers from released specifications.
tasks.enabler_now: Native material-structure expansion and contextual forms can reuse controlled job data.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual windings, ambiguous drawings, and unapproved substitutions require technical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises when a nominal material list does not match the physical coil variant.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated quantity derivation while preserving specification interpretation.

reach.learn: Which specification details must remain visible at the station

evidence.claim: Azumuta builds variant-specific instructions from manufacturing jobs, supporting controlled job-data presentation.
Native material expansion could replace repeated derivation for jobs with a released structured material list.

assumptions: The task includes source lookup, requirement derivation, interpretation, and preparation-note writing.

The production engineer produces job revision, part type, material identifier, per-unit quantity, unit, and valid variant in the released material structure; four other-role hours per 100 baseline hours cover maintaining this contract.
The operator verifies job identity and document revision in s1 and variant fit in s3. S4's eight retained hours include all substantive requirement and question capture.
Native views and forms are tested before custom code. If no released material structure exists, s2 stays manual with no saving; the design does not assume drawing extraction for free.
S4 saves formatting and repeated identifiers only; a same-system save receives no saving or self-approval gate. No machine send, substitute decision, or equipment command is proposed.
unknowns: How many coil variants have released structured material lists
Whether current job views already show expanded quantities
research_questions: Can native expansion match the operator's requirements for twenty representative jobs without missing variant details?

already_counted.description: Specification identity checks and variant judgement

incremental.description: Maintain job view configuration and investigate mapping failures

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 structured-variant scenario: B=100, R=25+0+40+8=73; gross 27%, less 6 focal upkeep gives central net 21%; conservative 0-10%. Four other-role hours are additional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select physical materials and load them onto coiling equipment.

steps.what: Look up available material lots for the required coiling workpieces
Select and verify physical workpieces, objects, and machine parts
Load selected materials onto coiling equipment safely

tasks.design: Configure a native available-lot view in {OPS_SYSTEM} for the selected material identifier. The operator still verifies the physical material and loads {OTHER} coiling equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated navigation through stock records can precede physical material selection.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved native filters can show relevant available lots without changing material acceptance or physical handling.
tasks.still_hard: Labels, condition, dimensions, and safe loading require direct checks.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises mismatched or damaged material before loading.
tasks.altitude: Make material-location lookup slightly quicker while retaining physical work.

reach.learn: Which stock-record delays cause wasted selection trips

evidence.claim: A native filtered lot view could reduce lookup navigation but cannot select or load physical material.

assumptions: The material-location lookup is included separately from selection and loading; no robot or automatic machine action is proposed.

Store personnel produce lot identifier, material identifier, available quantity, stock status, and storage location during existing receipt and movement work. No added entry duty is transferred; the operator checks physical identity within s2.
The view is a native read filter, not a new stock writer. Missing or stale records require manual location checks with no lookup saving.
Material requirements are derived once in task 11905; this step looks up physical lots rather than repeating specification review.
Operational recording is owned once by task 11908; no record write or send is hidden in physical loading. Same-system runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Whether available-lot navigation is already contextual
research_questions: Does a saved material filter reduce actual selection lookup time without extra stock upkeep?

already_counted.description: Material lookup and physical identity verification

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 navigation scenario: B=100, R=8+30+60=98; gross 2%, less 0.5 upkeep gives central net 1.5%; conservative 0-0.5%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record production and operational data on required forms.

steps.what: Identify the production job and capture operational counts and reasons
Copy production and operational data onto specified forms
Check production form completeness and correct source-entry errors

tasks.design: Configure a station form in {OPS_SYSTEM} that generates the required production form from once-captured operational entries. The operator identifies the job, captures facts and reasons, and checks the completed record.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same counts and job details may be copied from observations or counters onto separate specified forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Native station forms and report mappings can reuse source entries without retyping them.
tasks.still_hard: Scrap reasons and unusual interruptions require accurate operator observation.
tasks.human_edge: The operator distinguishes actual production events from counter artefacts or incomplete runs.
tasks.altitude: Record facts once and inspect a generated operational form.

reach.learn: Which fields are actually needed for traceability and planning

evidence.claim: Azumuta records scanner and test-equipment results and exchanges manufacturing identifiers with enterprise systems.
Evocon replaced paper reports and spreadsheets in the H+H case, supporting the digital reporting direction without a coil-winding time estimate.

assumptions: Observation, source entry, copying to required forms, and completeness checks are included; no recording work is excluded from an in-person step.

The operator produces job identifier, machine identifier, start/end time, output count, scrap count, reason code, and exception text in s1; its 40% share includes direct station entry and counter checks.
The production supervisor defines required fields, units, and form mapping; three other-role hours per 100 baseline hours cover maintaining that contract.
Native station capture and reporting are tried first. Missing counts or uncertain reasons remain for manual completion, not inferred values or automatic alerts.
S2 generates an internal form only; no enterprise send or separate commit is implied. Same-system saving has negligible effort and no saving credit. Existing automatic reports earn no new saving.
unknowns: How much current form work is repeated copying
Whether machine counters are reliable and accessible
research_questions: Can a native form reproduce required records with less total capture and checking time?

already_counted.description: Observation, job identification, and source capture
Form completeness review and source correction

incremental.description: Maintain form mapping and inspect failed source-entry patterns

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 duplicate-form scenario: B=100, R=40+0+20=60; gross 40%, less 8 focal upkeep gives central net 32%; conservative 0-20%. Three other-role hours are additional.

tasks.short: Examine and electrically test wired components, then record test results.

steps.what: Examine wired motors, armatures, and stators before electrical testing
Test wired electrical components using calibrated measuring devices
Record electrical test results against the component identifier
Check recorded test values and add examination findings or measurement exceptions

tasks.design: Use supported measuring-device capture in {OPS_SYSTEM}; {OTHER} denotes electrical measuring devices and their native export interface. The operator examines the component, performs the tests, and checks captured values and exception notes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copying instrument readings onto forms adds transcription work after the physical test.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported instrument exports can populate a component-linked test record.
tasks.still_hard: Connections, calibration, component condition, and ambiguous readings require direct operator checks.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises invalid measurements and decides when a test must be repeated.
tasks.altitude: Reduce test-value transcription while retaining physical examination and measurement judgement.

reach.learn: Which identity and calibration details are needed to reproduce a result

evidence.claim: Azumuta records results from connected test equipment, supporting device-to-record capture.
A supported test-device connection could remove value transcription without removing testing or checking.

assumptions: Physical examination, electrical testing, result recording, and checking are separate steps; test recording is not hidden inside testing.

The operator captures component identifier, test method revision, instrument identifier, and calibration reference during s1 and s2. The measuring device produces value, unit, channel, and time only after the actual test in s2; all identity capture and test preparation time remains counted there.
S3 requires a supported device export and component link. Missing identity, unsupported interfaces, or invalid values require manual recording with no saving.
Native instrument capture is tested before custom integration. No automatic pass/fail decision, alert, external send, or equipment command is proposed.

S4 retains annotation and correction time. Same-system saving has no self-approval gate or saving credit. These electrical test records are owned here once, distinct from production counts in task 11908.
unknowns: How component identity is linked before testing
Whether current test values are already captured automatically
research_questions: Can the supported connection capture identical values and units for known reference components without extra operator handling?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 manual-transcription scenario: B=100, R=20+40+0+15=75; gross 25%, less 6 upkeep gives central net 19%; conservative 0-10%. Already connected devices yield no new saving.
